answer: Each agent should earn influence only after completing a randomly assigned, verifiable task whose result is checked against a hidden test set, with rewards capped per credentialed participant. A Sybil attacker can still create many identities, but must spend real compute or labor on each one and risks losing it when outputs fail verification; cheap account creation alone buys no votes. For example, a task might classify terrace erosion in karst terrain from a pigment sample image, with hidden cases preventing copied answers from scaling.
